simple.meaning: רָבַע (râbaʻ) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “to squat or lie out flat, i.e. (specifically) in copulation.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 3 times across Leviticus, beginning at Leviticus 18:23. Its contexts include blood.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to רָבַע (H7250).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: רָבַע (râbaʻ) / H7250 is traced through Leviticus 18:23, Leviticus 19:19, Leviticus 20:16 as a generated source-based concept entry.

definitions.short: to squat or lie out flat, i.e. (specifically) in copulation
definitions.full: H7250. raba [ רָבַע ] verb lie stretched out, lie down (Aramaic form of רָבַץ (q. v.); Late Hebrew רבע usually of copulation, chiefly unnatural; yet compare also Sabean רבע abide, encamp, settle , DHM ZMG xxix (1875), 593 , Arabic abide, dwell ) — Qal only Infinitive: suffix רִבְעִי Psa 139:3 my lying down (for repose, opposed to אָרְחִי ); elsewhere (H) for copulation (woman with beast) אֹתָהּ לְרִבְעָה Lev 20:16 , but read אִתָּהּ (suffix of beast) Dr-Wh Kö Synt. 226 e , compare Bae Berthol (and Dr 2Sam 13:14 ); לְרִבְעָהּ 18:23 , read לְרִבְעָה (compl. omitted; see id. ). Hiph`il Imperfect 2masculine singular כִּלְאַיִם תַרְבִּיעַ לֹא בְּהֶמְתְּךָ Lev 19:19 (H) thy cattle thou shalt not cause to (let) lie down (i.e. breed) in two kinds.

occurrences.englishText: “ ‘You shall not lie with any animal to defile yourself with it. No woman may give herself to an animal, to lie down with it: it is a perversion.
“ ‘If a woman approaches any animal and lies with it, you shall kill the woman and the animal. They shall surely be put to death. Their blood shall be upon them.
